That being said, it is also important to put virtual currency in perspective as a payment

statutory.question: Does the conduct described fall within 5318(g)?
statutory.answer: No, 31 U.S.C. § 5318(g) requires reporting only for suspicious transactions, and the provided facts do not demonstrate suspicious activity.
statutory.label: contradiction
statutory.reasoning: 31 U.S.C. § 5318(g) requires financial institutions to report transactions that are 'suspicious,' typically meaning they have no apparent lawful purpose or are designed to evade reporting requirements. The fact pattern shows an individual with an expected monthly volume of $2,746 performing 20 transactions (out of 48 mentioned) ranging from approximately $67 to $293. The total volume of the listed transactions is well within the declared monthly throughput of a salaried wage earner. There are no indicators of structuring, rapid movement of funds, or anomalous counterparty behavior that would trigger a SAR. Because the activity is consistent with the KYC profile, 31 U.S.C. § 5318(g) requires reporting only for suspicious transactions which are not present here.
